qe: Which Article of the Constitution was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'Heart and Soul' of the Constitution?
qh: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर ने किस अनुच्छेद को संविधान का 'हृदय और आत्मा' कहा था?
e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar ne Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) ko 'Heart and Soul' kaha tha kyunki bina enforceable judicial remedies ke baaki sabhi Fundamental Rights sirf kagaz par reh jaate. Iske tehat citizen direct Supreme Court move kar sakta hai.

qe: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was the 'Right to Property' removed from the list of Fundamental Rights?
qh: 'संपत्ति के अधिकार' को किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा मौलिक अधिकारों की सूची से हटाया गया था?
e: Morarji Desai ki Janata Party government ne 44th Amendment Act 1978 ke zariye Article 19(1)(f) aur Article 31 ko repeal kar diya. Ab Right to Property Part XII ke Article 300A ke tehat sirf ek legal/constitutional right hai, fundamental right nahi.

qe: Which Fundamental Rights under Part III cannot be suspended even during a proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352?
qh: राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के दौरान भी भाग III के कौन से मौलिक अधिकार निलंबित नहीं किए जा सकते?
e: 44th Amendment Act 1978 ne Article 359 me amendment karke ye ensure kiya ki Article 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offenses) aur Article 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) ke enforcement ko emergency me bhi suspend nahi kiya ja sakta.

qe: Under Article 21A, the State is mandated to provide free and compulsory education to all children of which age group?
qh: अनुच्छेद 21A के तहत राज्य किस आयु वर्ग के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा देने के लिए बाध्य है?
e: 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002 ne Article 21A insert kiya, jo 6 se 14 saal ke sabhi bacchon ke liye elementary education ko fundamental right banata hai. Isko implement karne ke liye Right to Education (RTE) Act 2009 banaya gaya jo April 2010 se lagu hua.

qe: Which Writ is issued by constitutional courts to secure the release of a person who has been unlawfully detained?
qh: अवैध रूप से हिरासत में लिए गए व्यक्ति को रिहा कराने के लिए अदालत द्वारा कौन सी रिट जारी की जाती है?
e: Habeas Corpus ka literal meaning hota hai 'To have the body'. Ye writ public authorities aur private individuals dono ke khilaaf issue ho sakti hai agar detention bina kanooni justification ke ki gayi ho.

qe: Article 17 of the Constitution provides for the abolition of which social evil?
qh: संविधान का अनुच्छेद 17 किस सामाजिक बुराई के उन्मूलन का प्रावधान करता है?
e: Article 17 untouchability ko abolish karta hai aur iski kisi bhi form me practice ko forbid karta hai. Isko enforce karne ke liye Parliament ne Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 banaya hai. Ye ek absolute right hai jisme koi exception nahi hota.

qe: The concept of 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP) in Part IV was borrowed from the constitution of which country?
qh: 'राज्य के नीति निर्देशक तत्व' (DPSP) किस देश के संविधान से लिए गए हैं?
e: Indian Constitution ke Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) me shamil DPSP ko 1937 ke Irish Constitution se adopt kiya gaya tha, jisne ise Spanish Constitution se liya tha. Ye non-justiciable welfare guidelines hain.

qe: Article 44 of the Directive Principles directs the State to secure which uniform measure for all citizens?
qh: नीति निर्देशक तत्वों का अनुच्छेद 44 नागरिकों के लिए क्या सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश देता है?
o: Free legal aid across all courts
e: Article 44 states that the State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India, jo marriage, divorce, inheritance aur adoption ke personal laws me uniformity laane ke liye hai.

qe: Protection against 'Double Jeopardy' is guaranteed under which clause of the Constitution?
qh: 'दोहरे दंड' (Double Jeopardy) से संरक्षण किस अनुच्छेद के तहत प्रदान किया गया है?
e: Article 20(2) states: 'No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.' Ye protection sirf courts ya judicial tribunals ke aage hone wale prosecutions par apply hoti hai, departmental inquiry par nahi.

qe: Which Article of the Directive Principles mandates the State to separate the Judiciary from the Executive in public services?
qh: नीति निर्देशक तत्वों का कौन सा अनुच्छेद कार्यपालिका से न्यायपालिका को अलग करने का निर्देश देता है?
e: Article 50 state ko nirdesh deta hai ki criminal justice administration me judicial functions ko executive officers se separate kiya jaye taaki judicial independence aur fair trials ensure ho sakein.

qe: Under Article 19(1), how many fundamental democratic freedoms are currently guaranteed to Indian citizens?
qh: अनुच्छेद 19(1) के तहत वर्तमान में भारतीय नागरिकों को कितने प्रकार की स्वतंत्रताएं प्राप्त हैं?
e: Originally Article 19 me 7 freedoms thin. 44th Amendment Act 1978 dwara Article 19(1)(f) (property acquire karne ka right) delete hone ke baad ab 6 freedoms bachi hain: Speech, Assembly, Association, Movement, Residence aur Profession.

qe: Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution collectively guarantee which category of rights?
qh: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 25 से 28 सामूहिक रूप से किस श्रेणी के अधिकार की गारंटी देते हैं?
e: Articles 25 se 28 religious freedom protect karte hain: Article 25 (individual conscience & practice), Article 26 (religious affairs management), Article 27 (taxes for religion promotion se freedom), aur Article 28 (state-funded institutions me religious instruction se freedom).

qe: Under Article 39A, what constitutional mandate is imposed upon the State?
qh: अनुच्छेद 39A के तहत राज्य पर क्या संवैधानिक दायित्व सौंपा गया है?
o: To ensure equal pay for equal work
To provide free legal aid by suitable legislation to ensure justice is not denied due to economic disabilities
To enforce prohibition of intoxicating drinks
e: 42nd Amendment Act 1976 ke zariye Article 39A add kiya gaya, jo State ko equal justice aur free legal aid provide karne ka directive deta hai. Isko realize karne ke liye 1987 me NALSA Act banaya gaya.

qe: The concept of 'Rule of Law' incorporated in Article 14 was fundamentally derived from the constitutional jurisprudence of:
qh: अनुच्छेद 14 में शामिल 'कानून का शासन' (Rule of Law) की अवधारणा किस देश के न्यायशास्त्र से ली गई है?
e: Article 14 ka 'Equality before Law' British jurist A.V. Dicey ke Rule of Law principle par based hai, jiska matlab hai ki arbitrary power ka absence ho aur koi bhi vyakti kanoon se upar na ho. 'Equal protection of the laws' American Constitution se liya gaya hai.

qe: Under Article 23 of the Constitution, which specific exploitative practices are prohibited?
qh: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 23 के तहत किन शोषणकारी प्रथाओं पर रोक लगाई गई है?
o: Traffic in human beings, begar, and other similar forms of forced labour
e: Article 23 human trafficking, begar (bina remuneration ke kaam karwana) aur kisi bhi form ke forced labor ko prohibit karta hai. Iska violation law ke under ek punishable offense hai.

qe: Which Article of the Directive Principles serves as the constitutional foundation for India's foreign policy on international peace?
qh: नीति निर्देशक तत्वों का कौन सा अनुच्छेद अंतरराष्ट्रीय शांति पर भारत की विदेश नीति का आधार है?
e: Article 51 directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honorable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

qe: Under Article 24, children below what age are strictly prohibited from being employed in hazardous factories or mines?
qh: अनुच्छेद 24 के तहत किस आयु से कम के बच्चों को कारखानों या खानों जैसे जोखिम भरे कार्यों में नियोजित करने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध है?
e: Article 24 mandate karta hai ki 14 saal se kam age ke kisi bhi child ko kisi factory, mine ya hazardous employment me employ nahi kiya ja sakta. Ye ek absolute right hai jisme koi exception nahi hota.

qe: Which Landmark Case established the 'Basic Structure Doctrine', limiting Parliament's amending power under Article 368?
qh: किस ऐतिहासिक मामले ने 'मूल संरचना सिद्धांत' स्थापित कर अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत संसद की संशोधन शक्ति को सीमित किया?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
e: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) me 13 judges ki largest constitutional bench ne 7:6 ke majority se Basic Structure Doctrine di. Iske mutabiq Parliament Article 368 se Constitution amend toh kar sakti hai, par uske basic features (jaise Judicial Review, Democracy, Secularism) ko destroy nahi kar sakti.

qe: Article 15(1) prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on which specific grounds?
qh: अनुच्छेद 15(1) राज्य को अपने नागरिकों के खिलाफ किन विशिष्ट आधारों पर भेदभाव करने से रोकता है?
o: Only on grounds of Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, Place of birth or any of them
e: Article 15(1) me exactly 5 grounds mentioned hain: Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, aur Place of Birth. Isme 'Residence' (domicile) shamil nahi hai, isliye states higher education me local domicile ke base par quota de sakti hain.

qe: Under Article 22(2), an arrested individual must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within what maximum time window?
qh: अनुच्छेद 22(2) के तहत गिरफ्तार व्यक्ति को कितने समय के भीतर निकटतम मजिस्ट्रेट के समक्ष पेश किया जाना अनिवार्य है?
o: Within 24 hours (excluding journey time from place of arrest to court)
e: Article 22(2) ke mutabiq arrest ke 24 hours ke andar (journey time ko exclude karke) person ko magistrate ke aage produce karna compulsory hai. Magistrate ke judicial remand ke bina 24 hours se zyada custody me nahi rakha ja sakta.

qe: Article 30 confers the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions to which specific classes of citizens?
qh: अनुच्छेद 30 किन वर्गों को शैक्षणिक संस्थान स्थापित करने और उनका प्रशासन करने का मौलिक अधिकार प्रदान करता है?
o: Any section of citizens having a distinct language, script, or culture
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes exclusively
e: Article 30 exclusively minorities ke liye hai: 'All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.' Article 29 'any section of citizens' par apply hota hai.

qe: The writ of 'Mandamus' literally translates to which command, and against whom can it NOT be issued?
qh: 'परमादेश' (Mandamus) रिट का शाब्दिक अर्थ क्या है और यह किसके खिलाफ जारी नहीं की जा सकती?
o: 'We Command'; cannot be issued against the President of India or a State Governor
'To be Certified'; cannot be issued against lower courts
'By what Authority'; cannot be issued against municipal corporations
'To have the Body'; cannot be issued against police officers
e: Mandamus ka matlab 'We Command' hota hai, jo kisi public official ko statutory duty perform karne ke liye issue kiya jata hai. Article 361 ke constitutional immunities ke chalte ye President ya State Governor ke khilaaf unke official duties ke liye issue nahi ho sakta.

qe: Under Article 31C, which Directive Principles are given precedence over Fundamental Rights under Articles 14 and 19?
qh: अनुच्छेद 31C के तहत किन DPSP को अनुच्छेद 14 और 19 के मौलिक अधिकारों पर प्राथमिकता दी गई है?
o: Article 39(b) [distribution of material resources] and Article 39(c) [prevention of concentration of wealth]
e: 25th Amendment 1971 ke zariye add kiye gaye Article 31C ke tehat agar sarkar Article 39(b) aur 39(c) ke socialist wealth distribution ko enforce karne ke liye kanoon banati hai, toh use Articles 14 aur 19 ke violation ke ground par void declare nahi kiya ja sakta.

qe: Under Article 18, which specific titles are exempted from abolition and legally permitted to be retained?
qh: अनुच्छेद 18 के तहत किन विशिष्ट उपाधियों को प्रतिबंध से छूट दी गई है और उन्हें बनाए रखने की अनुमति है?
e: Article 18(1) states: 'No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.' Isliye Captain, Major, Doctor, Professor jaise merit-based titles permitted hain, jabki Rai Bahadur, Maharaja jaise titles banned hain.

qe: The constitutional mandate for the protection of forests and wildlife under Article 48A was added to the DPSP by which amendment?
qh: पर्यावरण और वन्यजीवों की सुरक्षा का संवैधानिक निर्देश (अनुच्छेद 48A) किस संशोधन द्वारा DPSP में जोड़ा गया था?
e: 42nd Amendment Act 1976 ke zariye DPSP me Article 48A joda gaya jo State ko environment protect/improve karne aur forests/wildlife safeguard karne ka directive deta hai. Isi amendment se 51A(g) me citizen ki fundamental duty bhi jodi gayi.

qe: The writ of 'Quo-Warranto' is issued by constitutional courts to inquire into:
qh: 'अधिकार पृच्छा' (Quo-Warranto) रिट संवैधानिक अदालतों द्वारा किसकी जांच के लिए जारी की जाती है?
o: The legality of a person's claim to a public substantive office created by charter or statute
The unlawful detention of an undertrial prisoner
The violation of natural justice by a tribunal
The refusal of an executive agency to disburse funds
e: Quo-Warranto ka matlab hota hai 'By what authority or warrant?'. Ye kisi person dwara public office hold karne ki statutory legality check karti hai taaki koi unqualified person illegal tarike se public chair occupy na kar sake.

qe: What does the 'Doctrine of Pith and Substance' determine in constitutional jurisprudence?
qh: संवैधानिक कानून में 'सार और तत्व का सिद्धांत' (Doctrine of Pith and Substance) क्या तय करता है?
o: Whether a state law is morally acceptable to the public
The true nature and character of a law to determine which legislative list of the Seventh Schedule it substantially falls under, despite incidental encroachments
The exact financial cost of implementing social legislation
The retrospective effect of civil statutes
e: Pith and Substance doctrine ye check karti hai ki kisi enactment ka core subject-matter (true nature and character) kis legislative list (Union, State ya Concurrent) ke andar aata hai. Agar law substantially apni list me hai, toh dusri list par minor incidental encroachment use invalid nahi banata.

qe: The Right to Education under Article 21A was incorporated into Part III primarily following the landmark judgment in which case?
qh: शिक्षा के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 21A) को मुख्य रूप से किस ऐतिहासिक मामले के फैसले के बाद भाग III में शामिल किया गया था?
o: Mohini Jain (1992) and Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
e: Mohini Jain case (1992) aur Unni Krishnan case (1993) me Supreme Court ne hold kiya tha ki Right to Education Article 21 ke Right to Life ka integral part hai. Is judicial interpretation ko statutory form dene ke liye Parliament ne 86th Amendment Act 2002 pass kiya.

qe: What did the 24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 clarify regarding Article 13 and constitutional amendments?
qh: 24वें संविधान संशोधन (1971) ने अनुच्छेद 13 और संविधान संशोधनों के संबंध में क्या स्पष्ट किया?
o: Constitutional amendments are completely void if they touch Fundamental Rights
Nothing in Article 13 shall apply to any amendment of the Constitution made under Article 368
The Supreme Court can strike down amendments without reason
State Legislatures must ratify all fundamental right amendments
e: Golaknath case (1967) me SC ne ruling di thi ki Article 368 ke tehat amendment bhi Article 13(2) ka 'law' hai, isliye FRs ko amend nahi kiya ja sakta. Isko counter karne ke liye 24th Amendment ne Article 13(4) add kiya jo ye establish karta hai ki Article 13 Article 368 amendments par apply nahi hoga.

qe: Under Article 35 of the Constitution, who alone is empowered to make laws prescribing punishments for acts declared to be offences under Part III (e.g., Articles 17 and 23)?
qh: अनुच्छेद 35 के तहत भाग III के अपराधों (जैसे अनुच्छेद 17 और 23) के लिए दंड निर्धारित करने का कानून बनाने का अधिकार केवल किसे है?
o: The Supreme Court through plenary guidelines
The Union Home Ministry through notifications
e: Article 35 ensure karta hai ki fundamental rights ke violations par penal laws poore desh me uniform hon. Isliye untouchability ya human trafficking par criminal penalties prescribe karne ki exclusive legislative authority sirf Parliament ke paas hai, State Assemblies ke paas nahi.

qe: What is meant by the 'Doctrine of Colorable Legislation' in Indian constitutional law?
qh: भारतीय संवैधानिक कानून में 'छद्म विधान का सिद्धांत' (Doctrine of Colorable Legislation) का क्या अर्थ है?
o: Legislation dealing with dyes and manufacturing
What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly; the legislature cannot overstep its constitutional jurisdiction under the guise of an apparent power
Laws enacted during wartime without debate
A statute that violates only the Preamble
e: Colorable legislation ka maxim hai 'Quando aliquid prohibetur ex directo, prohibetur et per obliquum' (jo directly nahi kiya ja sakta, wo ghumakar indirectly bhi nahi kiya ja sakta). Agar kisi legislature ke paas subject par direct power nahi hai, toh wo camouflage ya deceptive wording se use enact nahi kar sakti.

qe: Under Article 33 of the Constitution, Parliament is empowered to modify or restrict the application of Fundamental Rights to which category of personnel?
qh: अनुच्छेद 33 के तहत संसद को किस वर्ग के कर्मियों के मौलिक अधिकारों को सीमित करने की शक्ति प्राप्त है?
o: Members of the Armed Forces, forces charged with public order, intelligence organizations, and telecommunication systems set up for these forces
All employees of the central and state civil secretariats
Elected members of municipal councils and corporations
Only convicted undertrials lodged in state prisons
e: Article 33 Parliament ko power deta hai ki wo armed forces, police forces aur intelligence agencies ke personnel ke Fundamental Rights (jaise freedom of speech, association banana ya strike karna) ko restrict ya abrogate kare taaki discipline aur national defense compromised na ho.

qe: The 'Creamy Layer' exclusion principle for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in public employment was laid down in which landmark case?
qh: सरकारी नौकरियों में अन्य पिछड़े वर्गों (OBC) के लिए 'क्रीमी लेयर' को बाहर करने का सिद्धांत किस ऐतिहासिक मामले में तय किया गया था?
o: Champakam Dorairajan v. State of Madras (1951)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992 - Mandal Case)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
e: Indra Sawhney case (1992) me 9-judge bench ne 27% OBC reservation ko uphold kiya, par condition rakhi ki OBC community ke socially aur economically advanced section ('creamy layer') ko iska benefit nahi milega, aur total quota 50% limit cross nahi karega.

qe: Article 20(3) of the Constitution guarantees protection against 'Self-Incrimination'. What is its scope?
qh: अनुच्छेद 20(3) 'स्व-दोषारोपण' से संरक्षण प्रदान करता है। इसका दायरा क्या है?
o: No person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself in criminal proceedings
An accused cannot be compelled to give signature samples or thumb impressions
A witness is exempt from answering civil summons
A taxpayer cannot be audited by tax authorities
e: Article 20(3) state karta hai ki kisi bhi criminal accused ko khud ke khilaaf oral testimony ya incriminating confession dene ke liye compel nahi kiya ja sakta. Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010) me SC ne involuntary narco-analysis aur polygraph tests ko Article 20(3) ka violation mana.

qe: Under Article 22, what is the maximum duration for which a person can be detained under a Preventive Detention law without obtaining the opinion of an Advisory Board?
qh: अनुच्छेद 22 के तहत सलाहकार बोर्ड की अनुमति के बिना किसी व्यक्ति को निवारक निरोध कानून में अधिकतम कितने समय तक हिरासत में रखा जा सकता है?
e: Article 22(4) ke tehat preventive detention bina High Court judges ke Advisory Board ke review ke maximum 3 months tak hi continue ki ja sakti hai (44th Amendment ne ise 2 months karne ka provision kiya tha par wo clause notify nahi kiya gaya).

qe: In which landmark judgment did the Supreme Court explicitly establish that the Right to Privacy is a Fundamental Right under Article 21?
qh: किस ऐतिहासिक फैसले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने स्पष्ट रूप से स्थापित किया कि निजता का अधिकार अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत एक मौलिक अधिकार है?
o: Kharak Singh v. State of U.P. (1962)
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017)
Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)
e: August 2017 me 9-judge constitutional bench ne K.S. Puttaswamy case me unanimously hold kiya ki Right to Privacy ek intrinsic fundamental right hai jo Article 21 ke life and personal liberty aur Part III ke freedoms se emanate hota hai.

qe: Under Article 16(4A), who was provided reservation in matters of promotion with consequential seniority in public services?
qh: अनुच्छेद 16(4A) के तहत सरकारी सेवाओं में परिणामी वरिष्ठता के साथ पदोन्नति में आरक्षण किसे प्रदान किया गया?
e: 77th Amendment Act 1995 aur 85th Amendment Act 2001 ke zariye Article 16(4A) insert kiya gaya, jo State ko SC aur ST employees ke liye public services ke cadre me inadequate representation hone par reservation in promotion with consequential seniority dene ki power deta hai.

qe: What does the 'Doctrine of Severability' under Article 13(1) prescribe regarding unconstitutional statutory provisions?
qh: अनुच्छेद 13(1) के तहत 'पृथक्करणीयता का सिद्धांत' (Doctrine of Severability) क्या निर्धारित करता है?
o: The entire legislation is automatically voided if any single word conflicts with Fundamental Rights
Only the specific provision that is inconsistent with Fundamental Rights is declared void, provided the valid portion can operate independently
The law remains valid until Parliament reviews it within one year
The offending law is transferred to the Ninth Schedule
e: Doctrine of Severability kehta hai ki agar kisi statute ka unconstitutional part uske baki valid part se separate (sever) kiya ja sakta hai, toh poora act strike down karne ki zaroorat nahi hai; sirf offending portion void declare hoga.

qe: What does the 'Doctrine of Waiver' establish in Indian constitutional jurisprudence regarding Fundamental Rights?
qh: भारतीय संवैधानिक न्यायशास्त्र में 'त्याग का सिद्धांत' (Doctrine of Waiver) मौलिक अधिकारों के बारे में क्या स्थापित करता है?
o: A citizen can voluntarily surrender or waive their Fundamental Rights by signing a contract
A citizen CANNOT waive or give up any of their Fundamental Rights, as they are matters of public policy and constitutional obligation
The State can waive fundamental rights for government employees
Only corporate entities can waive constitutional rights
e: Behram Khurshed Pesikaka (1955) aur Basheshar Nath (1959) cases me Supreme Court ne rule kiya ki American law ke opposite India me koi bhi individual apne Fundamental Rights ko waive nahi kar sakta, kyunki Part III ke rights individual benefit ke sath-sath constitutional public policy ka mandatory part hain.

qe: What is the core procedural difference between the writ of 'Prohibition' and the writ of 'Certiorari'?
qh: 'प्रतिषेध' (Prohibition) और 'उत्प्रेषण' (Certiorari) रिट के बीच मुख्य प्रक्रियात्मक अंतर क्या है?
o: Prohibition is issued against executive officers, while Certiorari is issued against judges
Prohibition is preventive (issued while proceedings are pending to prevent excess of jurisdiction), whereas Certiorari is curative (issued after an order has been passed to quash an illegal decision)
Prohibition can only be issued by the Supreme Court, whereas Certiorari is exclusively issued by High Courts
Both writs perform identical functions without distinction
e: Prohibition trial ke chalte waqt lower judicial/quasi-judicial body ko jurisdiction exceed karne se rokne ke liye nikalti hai (preventive). Certiorari order pass hone ke baad jurisdictional error ya violation of natural justice hone par us illegal order ko quash karne ke liye nikalti hai (curative).

qe: Under Article 20(1), what constitutional protection is guaranteed against 'Ex-post facto laws'?
qh: अनुच्छेद 20(1) के तहत 'पूर्वव्यापी कानूनों' (Ex-post facto laws) के खिलाफ क्या सुरक्षा दी गई है?
o: No person can be convicted of any offense except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act, nor subjected to a penalty greater than that prescribed at that time
A person can be tried twice for the same offense if penalties are enhanced
Civil damages cannot be recovered retrospectively
Taxation laws can never be applied retroactively
e: Article 20(1) retroactive criminal legislation ko prohibit karta hai: kisi act ke commit hone ke baad use pichhli date se criminalize nahi kiya ja sakta aur na hi saza ko retrospectively badhaya ja sakta hai. Ye protection sirf criminal penal laws par apply hoti hai, civil liabilities ya taxes par nahi.

qe: In the landmark 'Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)' case, how did the Supreme Court revolutionize Article 21?
qh: 'मेनका गांधी मामले (1978)' में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने अनुच्छेद 21 की व्याख्या में क्या क्रांतिकारी बदलाव किया?
o: Held that the procedure depriving a person of life or personal liberty must be 'just, fair, and reasonable', effectively merging 'due process of law' into 'procedure established by law'
Restricted personal liberty to mere physical freedom from bodily restraint
Excluded foreign travel from the ambit of personal liberty
Declared that Fundamental Rights are mutually exclusive separate codes
e: A.K. Gopalan case (1950) ki narrow interpretation ko overrule karte huye Maneka Gandhi case (1978) me SC ne hold kiya ki procedure sirf statutory enactment nahi hona chahiye, balki natural justice ke standards par 'just, fair and reasonable' hona chahiye. Isne Articles 14, 19 aur 21 ke beech ka 'Golden Triangle' establish kiya.

qe: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 introduced which reservation provisions by amending Articles 15 and 16?
qh: 103वें संविधान संशोधन (2019) ने अनुच्छेद 15 और 16 में संशोधन करके क्या प्रावधान किए?
o: Up to 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment, over and above existing quotas
Horizontal 33% reservation for women in Parliament
Reservation for transgender communities in public sector units
e: 103rd Amendment Act 2019 ne Articles 15(6) aur 16(6) insert kiye, jinke tehat citizens ke Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) ko educational institutions aur initial public recruitment me up to 10% reservation diya gaya (Janhit Abhiyan case 2022 me ise SC ne constitutionally uphold kiya).

qe: Under Article 34 of the Constitution, what power is conferred upon Parliament when Martial Law is in force in any area?
qh: अनुच्छेद 34 के तहत किसी क्षेत्र में मार्शल लॉ लागू होने पर संसद को क्या शक्ति प्राप्त है?
o: Parliament may by law indemnify any person in the service of the Union or a State for acts done in connection with the maintenance or restoration of order
Parliament must surrender all fiscal powers to the army
The Supreme Court jurisdiction is abolished permanently
e: Article 34 Parliament ko power deta hai ki wo Indemnity Act pass karke military officers ya public servants dwara martial law ke dauran order restore karne ke liye kiye gaye acts ko legal protection de sake aur unke sentences/orders ko validate kar sake.

qe: In the 'Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012)' case, the Supreme Court recognized which basic human right as an integral component of Article 21?
qh: रामलीला मैदान मामले (2012) में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने किस अधिकार को अनुच्छेद 21 का अभिन्न अंग माना?
o: Right to sleep peacefully without arbitrary state disruption
Right to contest elections without party tickets
e: Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012) me mid-night police crackdown ko evaluate karte huye Supreme Court ne hold kiya ki 'Right to Sleep' human biological health aur dignity ke liye basic necessity hai aur ye Article 21 ke right to personal liberty ka essential part hai.

qe: What did the Supreme Court hold in 'Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)' regarding pavement dwellers?
qh: 'ओल्गा टेलिस मामले (1985)' में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने फुटपाथ पर रहने वालों के संबंध में क्या निर्णय दिया?
o: Pavement dwellers have no constitutional rights
The Right to Livelihood is an integral part of the Right to Life under Article 21, as no person can live without the means of living
Street vendors are exempt from civil municipal laws
e: Olga Tellis case (1985) me Chief Justice Y.V. Chandrachud ki bench ne rule kiya ki Article 21 ke Right to Life me 'Right to Livelihood' inherently included hai, kyunki kisi vyakti se uska rozgar aur ajeevika chheen lena uske jeene ke adhikar ko khatam karne ke barabar hai.

qe: Under Article 27 of the Constitution, what restriction is placed on the State regarding public revenues and religion?
qh: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 27 के तहत सार्वजनिक राजस्व और धर्म के संबंध में राज्य पर क्या रोक लगाई गई है?
o: The State cannot collect any municipal fees from religious shrines
No person shall be compelled to pay any taxes, the proceeds of which are specifically appropriated in payment of expenses for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion
Religious institutions are prohibited from holding bank accounts
Foreign donations to religious organizations are banned
e: Article 27 India ke secular character ko preserve karta hai: public tax money ko kisi specific religion ya denomination ko maintain ya promote karne ke liye use nahi kiya ja sakta. Lekin ye restriction 'tax' par hai, regulatory/service 'fees' (jaise pilgrim facilities ke charges) par nahi.

qe: What was established by the Supreme Court in the historic 'Champakam Dorairajan (1951)' case?
qh: 'चंपाकम दोराईराजन मामले (1951)' में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने क्या फैसला सुनाया जिसके कारण पहला संविधान संशोधन हुआ?
o: Communal caste-based quota in state medical colleges violated Article 29(2), leading Parliament to enact the First Constitutional Amendment adding Article 15(4)
e: Madras Government ke Communal G.O. (medical/engineering college quota) ko SC ne Article 29(2) ke discrimination ban ke ground par strike down kar diya. Is judgment ke baad Parliament ne First Constitutional Amendment Act 1951 pass karke Article 15(4) joda taaki SC/ST aur backward classes ke advancement ke liye special provisions banaye ja sakein.

qe: Under Article 19(1)(c), does the fundamental right to form associations or unions include the fundamental right to strike or declare lockouts?
qh: क्या अनुच्छेद 19(1)(c) के तहत संघ या यूनियन बनाने के अधिकार में हड़ताल (Strike) करने का मौलिक अधिकार भी शामिल है?
o: Yes, the right to strike is an absolute fundamental right
No, the right to form unions is a fundamental right, but the right to strike or lockout is merely a regulated legal/statutory right governed by industrial dispute statutes
e: All India Bank Employees' Association v. National Industrial Tribunal (1962) me SC ne clear kiya ki Article 19(1)(c) sirf association/union form karne ka right deta hai. Uske baad collective bargaining ke weapons (jaise strike ya lockout) Industrial Disputes Act ke tehat legal rights ho sakte hain, par Fundamental Right nahi hain.

qe: What is the crucial legal distinction between 'Equality before the Law' and 'Equal Protection of the Laws' under Article 14?
qh: अनुच्छेद 14 के तहत 'कानून के समक्ष समानता' और 'कानूनों के समान संरक्षण' के बीच क्या कानूनी अंतर है?
o: Both are identical concepts borrowed from France

'Equality before the law' (British origin) is a negative concept denoting absence of special privileges, whereas 'Equal protection of the laws' (American origin) is a positive concept demanding equal treatment of persons under similar circumstances
'Equal protection' applies only to foreign citizens
'Equality before law' applies only in military courts
e: Equality before Law (British origin) negative concept hai jo ye ensure karta hai ki koi bhi insaan kanoon se upar nahi hai. Equal Protection of Laws (American origin) positive concept hai jo 'reasonable classification' permit karta hai taaki like should be treated alike and unlike should not be treated alike (enabling affirmative action).
